prerequisites: Fundamentals of mathematical analysis (differential and integral calculus, function study)
economics and business organization (basics of investment analysis)

learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to provide knowledge of manufacturing plants through the fundamentals of design and maintenance of mechanical industrial plants and issues for managing the safety and health of operators employed in industrial settings.

The course, through the analysis of case studies referring to real plant systems and current technical and legislative regulations on occupational safety and health, will provide students with multiple evaluation tools that will enable them to properly apply the acquired knowledge in the design and maintenance of major non-complex mechanical industrial plants and the main tools for dealing with industrial safety management issues.

Through the study of alternative scenarios and decisive factors of choice, with reference to possible plant and organizational choices, the student will be able to refine technical knowledge and judgment in order to identify the best plant solutions referring to specific project scenarios, evaluate their inherent reliability and the associated risks involved.

The description of plant factors and risk analysis, with reference to integrated design techniques, will be carried out in a way that allows the acquisition of appropriate technical terminology. The development of oral and written communication skills will also be stimulated through classroom discussion of case studies and through the support of multimedia tools.

Learning skills will be stimulated through classroom discussions followed by an interactive student analytical process aimed at stimulating high levels of understanding of the topics covered. Learning skills will also be stimulated by various supplementary teaching aids, such as: design documents, specialized manuals, numerical exercises and industrial case studies, aimed at enhancing students' application skills.

syllabus_topics: Plant layout (1.5 CFU) Classification of industrial plants and production. Study of plant layout. Typological classification of layout. Production yields. Calculation of the number of layout operating units by departments. Quantitative methods in the study of layout by departments. Balancing of production lines.
Industrial buildings (1.5 CFU) Classification of industrial buildings. Construction types. Constituent parts. Interior lighting. Calculation of Primary Energy Requirement (FEP).
Material handling systems (1.5 CFU) Classification of internal transportation means. Loading units. Belt conveyors. Pneumatic conveyors. Hoists and winches. Augers. Bucket elevators. Trolleys.

Piping (1.5 CFU) Characteristic elements. Basic material selection and process design. Technical specification for component procurement. Assembly and protection of piping. Inspection and testing. Control system. Criteria for selecting a regulating valve. Operating characteristic of a regulating valve.

Systems reliability and maintenance (1.5 CFU) Non-repairable components. Time to failure, reliability, failure rates. Reliability evaluation. Repairable components. MTBF, MTTR and Availability. Functional and reliability diagrams. Series and parallel systems. Redundancy. Maintenance policies.

Fundamentals of work safety (1.5 CFU) Occupational safety legislation and guiding principles. Main regulatory references and figures of responsibility. Concepts of risk, harm, prevention, protection. Organization of corporate prevention. Occupational injury and occupational disease. Classification and statistics of accidents. Definition and process of risk assessment (ISO 14121). Risk analysis methodologies. DVR and DUVRI
teaching_methods: exercises supported by power point slides
tutoring in the form of individual assistance
assessment_rules: The examination comprises a written test for admission to a subsequent oral test. A mark of at least 18/30 in the written test is required for admission to the oral test. A minimum score of 18/30 is required to pass the oral test. Failure to participate in or pass the oral test invalidates the written test taken. The final grade represents an overall assessment of the student's preparation, as revealed by both the written test and the oral exam, based on criteria including knowledge, problem-solving ability, independent judgment, and technical language.
